frameworks_concepts.name: The Bitter Lesson
frameworks_concepts.summary: Sutton's thesis that general methods leveraging computation eventually beat methods leveraging human knowledge

frameworks_concepts.name: Era of Experience
frameworks_concepts.summary: Sutton's proposed paradigm: agents learn continually from a single stream of sensation, action, and reward

frameworks_concepts.name: Temporal-difference (TD) learning
frameworks_concepts.summary: Method for learning value functions from successive predictions, bridging short- and long-term reward

frameworks_concepts.name: Four-part agent model
frameworks_concepts.summary: Policy, value function, perception (state representation), and transition (world) model

frameworks_concepts.name: Big World Hypothesis
frameworks_concepts.summary: The world is too large to pre-program; agents must learn the idiosyncratic specifics in deployment

frameworks_concepts.name: Catastrophic interference
frameworks_concepts.summary: Deep nets overwrite old skills when trained on new ones — symptom of bad generalization

frameworks_concepts.name: Imitation vs. trial-and-error learning
frameworks_concepts.summary: Sutton's claim that animal learning is fundamentally trial-and-error and prediction, not imitation

frameworks_concepts.name: AI succession
frameworks_concepts.summary: The thesis that more-capable digital or augmented intelligences will inevitably take over from biological humans
